evidence.claim: ACTUS, loans, swaps, vaults and other applications are libraries/examples; supported constructs compose into arbitrary new programs.
U6 retains ACTUS fixtures/fields, DeFi rows, held-outs, independent expectations and separate semantic/native/local/Preview coverage.
U5 depends on U3 and applicable U4 history/privacy evidence.
U6 depends on U2 plus applicable U3/U4/U5 interfaces per family.
U0 profile covers only primitives already implemented by successor; AMM, vault and ACTUS arithmetic remain U6.
Canonical prices are base-per-quote; reciprocal source adaptation requires dimensioned conversion.
Protocol-favoring ceil for owed/liability amounts, floor for received amounts; remainder to protocol reserve; overrides explicit.
162 cases: 87 accepted and 75 rejected; expected outcomes prepared independently of execution.
The local consumer checks all 23 primary actions, complete poststate, asset/party identities, duties and ordered effects.
Quint model is a component toward M11; full M11 and Capacity Exchange remain open.
FeePool is a finite one-epoch source component with fixed roster/receipt shape.
Full M11, Capacity Exchange, general registries, native custody correspondence and financial acceptance remain open.
Inputs and 32 numeric predecessor fields must be below 2^64; quotient/remainder witnesses checked with checked Core u128.
Example funds gross amount, records costs/stipends, splits surplus and holds watcher reserve.
Financial example has two same-recipient payments, separate fee, accrued duty and repayment residual checks.
These are compilation examples and make no ledger-effect claim.
Static compilation checks profile/action limits and builds action groups.
Relation compiler names per-step before/after liability frame inputs.
Compiler includes typed liability before/after fields; this does not itself supply conditional recovery lifecycle.
Ordinary logical work excludes protected recovery slice.
DUST economics are staged separately; logical work is retained even when interpretation fails.
Unknown finality retains hold; timeout does not release it.
Capability scope binds grant, network, anchor, program, action, beneficiary and DUST cap.
FeeCapability stores scoped identity, cap, spent amount and reservation states.
Unknown or finalized holds cannot be released based only on timeout.
Policy has network, anchor, epoch, role grants and revoked IDs.
Authorization checks quorum, unique members, membership, revocation and call scope.
U5 also requires common evidence statement, federation rules, migration, adapters, OWS/x402, durable reservations, two solvers, and direct-use independence.
U3 requires two-asset escrow, recipient/document conditions, partial fill, persistent duties, continuation, joins, race controls, separate recovery authority and state-cap boundary.
Local K comparison and scoped Preview results are foundations; lifecycle gaps remain.
Whole-language audit found recovery reserve/lifetime gaps; architecture proposal does not repair implementations.
Successor repayment helper is a narrow reference primitive, not full loan/ACTUS family coverage.
ACTUS retains 277 fixtures, expected fields, 18 executable types, 32 taxonomy dispositions and DS01-07.
DeFi retains 72 original rows, DA01-24, supplementary cases, held-outs, intents and regression classes; batching cannot reduce denominator.
M11 expressly includes both FeePool and Capacity Exchange contracts, scoped reservation/settlement, native tests and integration readback.
M12 requires versioned per-block anchors, authenticated membership/roles, freshness, count/root, history and missing-anchor refusal.
M13 includes pending/partial/unknown/settled/recovered, residual duties, caps, late success, timeout, cancellation and compensation.
M14 preserves gross/fees/net/liabilities and rejects unsupported cross-domain atomicity.
M15 specifies batch clearing, uniform price, solver bounds, oracle freshness/authority and conservative liquidation.
M16 requires four separated cost planes, protected recovery work and cumulative caps; source sponsor implements only local scoped subset.
M17 requires actual committee identity, role separation, quorum/key commitments, rotation/revocation and acceptance conditions.
Later U6 libraries must declare any per-primitive rounding overrides explicitly.
Every financial family needs scope matrix, independent expectations and held-out compositions.
Federated kernel is optional; Moriarty can run on Midnight without federation.
Clock/import/governance are premises; finite source cases do not establish authenticated import, native custody or full M11.
Payments/escrow and asynchronous/conditional claims are retained library families.
Shares and vaults are retained library families; stable-time conversion is not accrual.
Netting, redemption/loss allocation and margin are retained library families.
Loans and claims are retained library families.
ACTUS cash-flow contracts are retained library family.
Swaps and liquidity/AMMs are retained family; narrow token0 pricing is not full AMM.

coverage_gaps: This is a bounded semantic map, not exhaustive structural inventory or a predicate denominator audit.
ACTUS, DeFi, AMM, vault, margin, redemption/loss allocation, netting, async escrow and other broad families are specified beyond the FeePool/payment-duty concrete sources inspected.

No evidence here qualifies native financial settlement, authenticated state/time/imports, complete actual ledger duties, DUST, Preview full financial acceptance, recursion/private multi-parent handoff, or release.

Profile claims are exact to the source examples: FeePool one epoch/two operator seats/one DA seat/one watcher, fixed ordinary/stipend/reserve receipt slots; U64 inputs and 128-bit checked products. It is not general financial language coverage.

Current public source-static call compilation uses explicit named profiles; unsigned mapped roles are only an opt-in static source compilation form, while legacy unsigned and signed/native paths preserve single-payer constraints (examples/core/fee-pool/README.md:154-158).
The historical Fenrir M11-M17 table is a target specification; M labels do not assert current implementation or acceptance.
questions_for_audit: For each retained family, define independent source expectation, exact primitive/rounding/unit profile, allowed source constructs, held-outs, and separate local/native/Preview denominator; how will every original ACTUS/DeFi count remain visible?

Can M11 be decomposed into FeePool source economics, authenticated importer/registry, separate Capacity Exchange stream, native custody relation, and integration readback, each with a conjunctive exit?

What concrete two-asset U3 program exposes partial fill, residual duty, recipient/document condition, join, late success versus refund, separate revocation/scoped recovery, reserve exhaustion and terminal consumption?

Which exact profile and source digest establish that a library is admitted: legacy source, source-static/native-call, signed owner-intent, local evaluator, or Preview ledger? How are claims prevented from crossing profiles?
What arithmetic oracle audits price orientation, directed rounding, dust beneficiary, gross versus net, overflow and field/finite-width mismatch across every library primitive?
For M16, where are logical work, circuit/protocol DUST, service and external costs charged and reconciled atomically under concurrent retries and unknown finality?
For M17, what authenticated policy gives membership/key commitments and epoch migration while preserving duties, replay state, and already consumed authority?

Which requirements are actually implemented in generic source/Core, which only exist as reference examples/models, and which are prose-only? Require file-level traceability plus a working consumer for every claimed library capability.
Which M12 registry/anchor system is normative, and how does its per-block freshness differ from inherited 60-second upstream assumptions?
How will reviewers distinguish a valid local finite example from general library coverage and avoid treating case counts as independent family breadth?
